claims.quote: This is done by making the hours of labor in different trades to differ according to their arduousness.
claims.description: A national labor administration balances the appeal of trades by giving harder jobs shorter working hours, adjusted by volunteer rates.

claims.quote: the administration would only need to take it out of the common order of occupations by declaring it 'extra hazardous,' and those who pursued it especially worthy of the national gratitude, to be overrun with volunteers.
claims.description: Dangerous necessary jobs are filled by declaring them 'extra hazardous' and honoring those who do them.

claims.quote: Health and safety are conditions common to all industries.
claims.description: All industries are made healthy and safe; workplace injury and unhygienic conditions are abolished.

claims.quote: Every one, indeed, is expected to study his aptitudes so as to have not only a first choice as to occupation, but a second or third
claims.description: Every worker holds ranked first, second and third occupational choices in case invention or demand displaces them.

claims.quote: holds always in reserve the power to call for special volunteers, or draft any force needed from any quarter.
claims.description: The state can draft workers into any trade when volunteers fall short.

claims.quote: It is the grade to which all new recruits belong for the first three years of their service.
claims.description: All young people serve three years as general unskilled laborers in a national industrial service before choosing a trade.

claims.quote: every worker is allowed, of course, under certain regulations and in accordance with the exigencies of the service, to volunteer for another industry which he thinks would suit him better than his first choice.
claims.description: Workers may transfer to another industry or region under regulation.

claims.quote: we leave the question whether a man shall be a brain or hand worker entirely to him to settle.
claims.description: Each person freely chooses whether to be a professional or a manual worker after the three-year service.

claims.quote: The schools of technology, of medicine, of art, of music, of histrionics, and of higher liberal learning are always open to aspirants without condition.
claims.description: Free national professional and higher-education schools are open to all without condition.

claims.quote: Our schools are national institutions, and to have passed their tests is a proof of special abilities not to be questioned.
claims.description: Professional qualification comes only from national schools whose diplomas certify real ability.

claims.quote: remains open to every man till the age of thirty is reached, after which students are not received, as there would remain too brief a period before the age of discharge in which to serve the nation in their professions.
claims.description: Professional training is open until age thirty, and national service ends at a fixed age of discharge.

claims.quote: Since the nation is the sole employer, the government must fix the rate of wages and determine just how much everybody shall earn, from the doctors to the diggers.
claims.description: The nation is the sole employer of all workers.

claims.quote: which was fastened with a slightness indicating that burglary was not among the perils of the modern Boston
claims.description: Burglary has effectively vanished from the future Boston.

claims.quote: But I think what surprised me as much as anything was not to find any stores on Washington Street, or any banks on State.
claims.description: Shops and banks have disappeared from the city.

claims.quote: Their functions are obsolete in the modern world.
claims.description: Merchants and bankers have been abolished as obsolete occupations.

claims.quote: There is neither selling nor buying nowadays; the distribution of goods is effected in another way.
claims.description: Buying and selling between individuals no longer exist.

claims.quote: As to the bankers, having no money we have no use for those gentry.
claims.description: Money has been abolished.

claims.quote: A system of direct distribution from the national storehouses took the place of trade, and for this money was unnecessary.
claims.description: The nation is the sole producer, and goods are distributed directly from national storehouses instead of through trade.

claims.quote: A credit corresponding to his share of the annual product of the nation is given to every citizen on the public books at the beginning of each year, and a credit card issued him with which he procures at the public storehouses, found in every community, whatever he desires whenever he desires it.
claims.description: Every citizen receives an annual credit, an equal share of national output, and spends it with a credit card at public storehouses.

claims.quote: The term, as we use it, answers to no real thing, but merely serves as an algebraical symbol for comparing the values of products with one another.
claims.description: The 'dollar' survives only as an abstract accounting unit, not real money.

claims.quote: The value of what I procure on this card is checked off by the clerk, who pricks out of these tiers of squares the price of what I order.
claims.description: Purchases are recorded by punching the amount out of a grid of squares on a pasteboard credit card.

claims.quote: our credit would not be transferable, being strictly personal.
claims.description: Citizens' credit is strictly personal and cannot be transferred to others.

claims.quote: we can obtain a limited advance on the next year's credit, though this practice is not encouraged, and a heavy discount is charged to check it.
claims.description: Citizens may draw a discouraged, discounted advance on next year's credit.

claims.quote: Of course if a man showed himself a reckless spendthrift he would receive his allowance monthly or weekly instead of yearly, or if necessary not be permitted to handle it all.
claims.description: Spendthrifts get their allowance in weekly or monthly installments or have it managed for them.

claims.quote: it is presumed that the citizen who does not fully expend his credit did not have occasion to do so, and the balance is turned into the general surplus.
claims.description: Unspent annual credit returns to the national surplus.

claims.quote: No man any more has any care for the morrow, either for himself or his children, for the nation guarantees the nurture, education, and comfortable maintenance of every citizen from the cradle to the grave.
claims.description: The nation guarantees every citizen's upbringing, education and comfortable living from cradle to grave.

claims.quote: But now it would have no such laudable object, and, having lost its utility, it has ceased to be regarded as a virtue.
claims.description: With universal economic security, thrift and saving are no longer considered virtues.

claims.quote: But you see it is a good deal of a jolt to drop a hundred years
claims.description: A man from the nineteenth century sleeps for over a century and wakes in the year 2000.
